主要内容: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on March 4, 2015, that short- and long-term disability insurance programs help replace some of the wages lost by workers unable to work due to non-work-related injuries or illnesses. In 1999, 36% of private industry workers had short-term disability insurance, rising to 39% by 2014. Long-term disability insurance coverage increased from 25% in 1999 to 33% in 2014. Workers in service occupations had the lowest rates of coverage, with only 19% having short-term disability insurance and 10% having long-term coverage in 2014. In contrast, workers in management, professional, and related occupations had the highest rates, with 53% and 57% respectively. These data are from the National Compensation Survey-Benefits program. For more details, see the February 2015 edition of Beyond the Numbers by Kristen Monaco.
